title: Masquerading: Rename System Utilities (T1036.003)
text: Adversaries rename legitimate system utilities such as certutil.exe, rundll32.exe, mshta.exe, or powershell.exe to evade security monitoring that keys on the utility name or Image path. Copying a signed LOLBin to an innocuous or business-looking filename (e.g. AdobeUpdater.exe), or relocating it to a non-standard directory, bypasses detection controls that rely on the on-disk name/path. Procedure examples: APT38 renamed rundll32.exe and mshta.exe to avoid detection; Daggerfly used a renamed rundll32.exe called dbengin.exe in ProgramData to proxy malicious DLL execution. Detection guidance: monitor for execution where the on-disk filename does not match PE metadata OriginalFileName / InternalName, rather than relying on the Image path alone. This is the canonical evasion for LOLBin download rules anchored on Image.
